ops.title: 2026-07-14 yasyf-home FP bridge outage — b.sock wedged/unbindable after companion-app death; acct-12..16 retreated to symlink as the unblock; acct-11 left on FP with upstream sync queued

ops.body:
2026-07-14 on yasyf-home (ccp v0.53.0, app cask 0.52.0): all 6 hostsync-materialized FP accounts (acct-11..16, created Jul 13 22:11+ by the origin-owned-sync migration) served enumeration but failed content materialization (EDEADLK, files SF_DATALESS). acct-11 only "worked" because a 02:38 session had fully hydrated it. Root sequence: the CCPoolStatus companion app died at 04:21 and the daemon-side group-container bridge (b.sock in `SXKCTF23Q2.ccp`, DAEMON-bound; the appex is the client — `internal/daemon/fileprovider.go` startFPBridge/serveFPBridge) wedged bound-but-dead — still holding the socket but serving nothing; after a daemon restart the bind is permission-parked (`os.ErrPermission` → the "awaiting app-group-container consent" hint, which is accurate for this state). Subtlety: TCC AppData rows for `/Users/yasyf/.cc-pool/bin/cc-pool` EXIST (written Jul 13 22:12 PDT — `datetime(...,'unixepoch')` prints UTC; don't misread TCC timestamps) yet the launchd bind is still denied — rows-on-disk ≠ effective grant; the successful bind yesterday came one second after a foreground/GUI-context approval. `ccp fp repair` (re-register) rides the separate control plane (`domains.sock`, APP-bound) so it can't fix a dead content bridge; `ccp fp onboard` spins at "waiting for the CCPoolStatus app" even while the app serves domains.sock.

**Why:** distinguishes the FP failure layers — domain replica (fp repair fixes), daemon content bridge (only a working b.sock bind+serve fixes; can be bound-but-dead with NO hint at all), and launchd-suppressed group-container consent (rows may exist yet not be effective) — control-plane ✓s (doctor, fp repair) prove nothing about the data plane.

**How to apply:** for FP reads failing on never-hydrated accounts, `ccp fp repair --retreat --account N` is the safe unblock when the account is all-dataless + session-free (nothing local to lose). Leave hydrated live-session FP accounts alone (their reads work; upstream sync queues until the bridge heals). Afterward accounts sit on symlink until `ccp migrate --to fileprovider` — only re-migrate after the bridge bug is fixed. Full incident: cc-notes note "yasyf-home FP bridge outage 2026-07-14". Related: [[fp-backend-rollout]], [[origin-owned-sync-shipped-v0530]], [[macos-tcc-identifier-keying]].
